payload.name: silicon (diamond cubic)
payload.structure_source: ideal diamond structure (Fd-3m, A4), built with ase.build.bulk
payload.rationale: Requested system: equilibrium lattice constant of diamond-cubic Si from an E(V) equation-of-state fit.

_fulfilled_need.query: Compute the equilibrium lattice constant of diamond-cubic silicon from an equation-of-state fit.

summary: candidate silicon (diamond cubic) (elemental semiconductor, trust tier)

method.engine: mace-torch 0.3.15 MACECalculator via ASE 3.29 (in the ALCHEMI toolkit env, NVIDIA GB10 GPU)
method.protocol: static 0 K E(V) scan: rigid isotropic scaling of ideal diamond cell (both atoms on fixed symmetric sites, so no internal relaxation is needed), fit with Birch-Murnaghan / Murnaghan / Vinet / Stabilized-jellium (ase.eos); strain windows +-2% (11 pts), +-4% (15 pts), +-6% (21 pts) in a; 2-atom primitive and 8-atom conventional cells
method.ensemble: none (static lattice, 0 K, no zero-point or thermal expansion)
method.fit_spread_angstrom: 5.4654-5.4673 across all EOS forms and windows; 2-atom and 8-atom cells identical to 1e-5
method.validation: Same protocol on diamond C: 3.578 A vs PBE 3.573 / exp 3.567. On Ge: 5.720 A vs PBE 5.785 / exp 5.652. References: arXiv:2010.13050, PBE lattice-constant table (PBE values: C 3.573, Si 5.467, Ge 5.785; exp: 3.567, 5.430, 5.652).

payload.note: Result: a0 = 5.466 A (BM, +-4% window: 5.4666 A). What it is: the static-lattice (0 K, no zero-point motion) PBE-level lattice constant, since MACE-MPA-0 is trained on PBE/PBE+U data (MPtrj + sAlex). Premise check: well-defined and appropriate; EOS fit to a perfect periodic crystal, so system size and timescale do not matter (2- and 8-atom cells give identical results). Validation: the model reproduces the literature PBE Si value 5.467 A to 0.001 A, and diamond C to within 0.005 A of PBE. Ge is 0.065 A (1.1%) below the cited PBE value, but PBE Ge values in the literature depend on how the 3d semicore states are treated. So the model's agreement with PBE is not uniformly better than about 1% across group IV, and Si (heavily represented in training) agrees best. Uncertainty +-0.005 A: covers the EOS-form and fit-window spread (+-0.001 A) plus model-vs-PBE error estimated from the C/Si validation. It does NOT cover the systematic PBE functional error versus experiment. Comparison with experiment: CODATA 2018/2022 Si lattice parameter 5.431020511(89) A at 22.5 C in vacuum (NIST). Our value is +0.035 A (+0.65%) above it, which is the well-known PBE overestimate. It is not a fit or model failure. Zero-point and thermal corrections to 295 K are small for Si (a few mA at most, not computed here). Use 5.431 A if the experimental room-temperature value is what you need.
